brief: Tonight is Pull B, your third day in a row, and it is a rep night more than a weight night. Almost nothing gets heavier. The Smith row stays exactly where it was — 115, 135, 145, 150 — but you have stopped every single set on exactly 8 reps for two Pull B sessions running, and 8 is the bottom of the range, so the bar has not earned another plate. Tonight the ask is 10, 10, 9, 9. Get those and it earns weight next week. Same idea on the shrugs: stay on the 70s and go 14, 13, 13, because the rack has nothing between 70 and 80 and you were doing 70 for 15s in December, so this is ground you have already held. Same on the last set of incline curls, where you keep getting 10, 10 and then dropping to 8 — all three need to reach 10 before we go near the 30s, so take the extra rest before that last one. Two sets get their light warm-up weight deleted: the lat pulldown starts at 120 now and the reverse curl at 37.5, because you already did both of those for full reps last time and the easy opener was not earning anything. The only real load increase tonight is face pulls, 27.5 up to 28.75 — that is one of the small round add-on weights on each handle. You missed reps at 27.5 twice and then got a clean 15 and 15 last night, so it is done. Two cues. On the row, end the set when your lower back starts doing the pulling, not when your arms quit. On the straight-arm pulldown, 37.5 stays until all three sets clear 12 — the next notch up is a big jump and there is nothing in between. Cardio: you have logged one 15-minute session since the 21st and the plan asks for two or three easy 20-to-30-minute sessions a week, so put one in tomorrow. Last thing, and it is the most important thing on this card: step on the scale tonight and tap the number in. See the notice below.

flags.note: You have weighed in once since January — 206 on July 21, down from 214 on January 4. You are in a build block, so weight drifting down is the wrong direction. Weigh in tonight and once a week from here, because right now I am guessing.

Face pulls have been in six of your last eight sessions, and yesterday added three sets of reverse pec deck on the same rear shoulders. Tonight's two sets stand — tell me if they feel cooked and we will thin them out.
Third training day in a row, which is what the plan asks for. You are on day 3 of 6 before your next rest day.

overrides.reason: Same weights as last time. You stopped on exactly 8 reps on every set two Pull B sessions running, so the bar has not earned more — do 10, 10, 9, 9 and it earns it next week.
Your light opener at 112.5 hit 12 reps, the top of the range, so it moves up to 120. You already did 120 for 10 twice last time, so all three sets run there now.
Stay on the 70s — the rack has nothing between 70 and 80, so reps are the only lever here. You held 70 for 15, 15, 15 in December, so 14, 13, 13 is inside what you have already done.
Weight stays at 25. You get 10 and 10 and then fall to 8 on the third set — finish all three at 10 and the 30s are next. Take extra rest before that last set if you need it.
Drop the light 32.5 opener. You did 37.5 for 12 on both work sets last time, so start there and run all three sets at 37.5.
Up from 27.5 to 28.75 — add one small round add-on weight to each handle. You missed reps at 27.5 twice and then got a clean 15 and 15 last night, so it is earned.

panel.note: The program seat did not report this morning — it was interrupted twice and wrote no file. It carries no load authority, so tonight's numbers are unaffected, but no structure recommendations were reviewed today.

dissent.progression: He finally cleared 27.5 for a clean 15 and 15 last night after missing it twice, and on a fixed-15-rep lift the weight is the only thing that can move — go to 28.75.
dissent.recovery: Cut to a single set at 27.5: face pulls have appeared in six of his last eight sessions, and yesterday added three hard sets of reverse pec deck on the same rear shoulders.
dissent.why: Recovery labelled this one itself — it wrote that the cut was redundancy, not fatigue. That makes it an argument about how the week is composed, and composition never moves a number on the night; it goes to the athlete as a question instead, which is why it is in the flags. Recovery filed no veto and reported his rest times tightening across the week, so there is no fatigue case to set against the load. Meanwhile progression's read is exact and I checked it: 15 and 12 on the 23rd, 15 and 14 on the 24th, 15 and 15 clean on the 27th. Handing him 27.5 a fourth time is the copy-paste this panel exists to stop, and 28.75 is the smallest step this machine physically has.

dissent.progression: Keep three sets at 70 and raise the reps to 14, 13, 13 — the rack has nothing between 70 and 80, so reps are the only lever this lift has.
dissent.recovery: Drop to two sets at 70 for 12: his reps fell from 14 to 12 when he went from 60 to 70 last Pull B, and his traps held 120 overhead yesterday.
dissent.why: I checked the claim under each side. Recovery is right that the reps fell on the jump to 70 — but that was his first session back at 70 this July, and the longer log shows 70 for 15, 15, 15 in December and again in January, and 70 for 14, 14, 14 in February. So 14, 13, 13 is not new ground, it is ground he has already held. Cutting the third set would delete the only progression lever this lift has, in a week where recovery itself found no fatigue and filed no veto. Yesterday's overhead press holds the traps still rather than working them through a range, which costs less than it looks.

dissent.progression: Hold all four weights and prescribe 10, 10, 9, 9 — he has never once finished a set above the bottom of the 8-to-10 range.
dissent.recovery: Repeat last Pull B exactly at 8 reps across, and earn reps inside the window before any weight goes on — it is the heaviest thing on his lower back the day after overhead pressing.
dissent.why: This is closer to agreement than it looks, and I ruled the way that honours both. Neither seat wants more weight, and recovery's own instruction was to earn reps in the 8-to-10 window first. Writing the rep target onto the card is what makes that ask real instead of a hope — leave it blank and he repeats 8s for a third session and nothing ever moves. The load on his lower back is identical either way.

dissent.progression: The 112.5 opener hit 12 reps, the top of the range, so it moves to 120 and all three sets run there — he already did 120 for 10 twice last time.
dissent.recovery: Repeat last time exactly; he got 12 on the first set but only 10 on the next two, and he has just corrected how that station is set up, so give him one clean session before changing anything.
dissent.why: The setup note recovery leaned on was about the cable row on Pull A, not this pulldown, so it is one step removed from tonight's lift. And this is not new weight: 120 is a load he completed for 10 twice in the same session last week, and he carried 127.5 for three sets through January and February. Raising the opener to match his own working sets is the smallest honest change on the board.

dissent.progression: Drop the 32.5 opener and run all three sets at 37.5 — he already did 37.5 for 12 on both work sets last time.
dissent.recovery: Repeat last time as logged, including the 32.5 opener, and push the reps up instead.
dissent.why: Recovery asked for more reps but named no number, and on a lift he has finished at exactly 12 for two sessions running, an unwritten ask changes nothing. The concrete change available is the light first set, which is proven work he cleared twice last week. It is a small forearm lift with 75 seconds of rest, and recovery itself reported his rest on this one was right on target, so there is no fatigue cost to weigh against it.
